eventMetadata.context_description:
**Mid-winter climatology and short-range forecast guidance position 14–15°C as the most probable maximum temperature range for Buenos Aires on June 13, 2026.** 

Typical June daily highs average 14–16°C under the influence of the South Atlantic subtropical high, with variability driven by cold fronts, cloud cover, and wind patterns that can suppress or enhance daytime warming. Recent model consensus from sources including SMN Argentina and international guidance shows a high near 15°C, with overnight lows around 9°C and light precipitation or overcast skies limiting solar heating. This aligns with observed trends on prior days (e.g., 18°C on June 11) shifting toward cooler conditions, keeping 13–15°C outcomes dominant in trader pricing. Uncertainty stems from potential model divergence on exact cloud timing and frontal passage, which could nudge the peak by 1°C either way before official SMN observations finalize resolution.

The low probabilities assigned to 34°C+ or sub-30°C outcomes reflect the narrow envelope created by these thermodynamic constraints and the timing of convective initiation. eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts for Paris on June 14 point to mostly clear skies under building high pressure, with daytime maxima expected between 25–27°C depending on the model run and exact station. Météo-France guidance and ensemble outputs cluster near 26°C, while some private models like Meteored push toward 30–31°C; traders appear to weight official consensus and recent cooler trends more heavily. Key variables include afternoon mixing depth, light northerly winds, and urban heat-island effects that can add 1–2°C locally. With 25°C and 26°C outcomes nearly tied in implied probability, the market reflects genuine uncertainty in final model consensus ahead of tomorrow’s peak heating. Updated guidance from Météo-France and NWP runs will likely resolve the narrow spread.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Denver’s June 14 high temperature centers on a cooler-than-normal day driven by an incoming weather system.** Official National Weather Service guidance and recent model consensus point to mostly cloudy skies with a chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms, limiting daytime heating and producing a forecast high near 68–70 °F—well below the early-June climatological normal of ~82 °F.

Key differentiating factors among the tightly bunched leading bins (70–71 °F at 25.6 %, 68–69 °F at 20.5 %, 72–73 °F at 17.1 %) include the precise timing and coverage of cloud build-up, the efficiency of any showers in enhancing evaporative cooling, and subtle differences in low-level wind direction that modulate downslope warming from the Rockies. Stronger or earlier cloud cover and precipitation tilt the outcome toward the 68–69 °F range, while partial clearing or delayed convection supports the upper end of the 70–73 °F cluster. Higher-temperature bins (>74 °F) carry low implied probabilities because they would require unexpectedly rapid clearing or stronger downslope flow not currently favored by guidance.

The market reflects aggregated trader assessment of these short-term forecast uncertainties, with the narrow spread underscoring how sensitive the final verified high will be to the exact evolution of the system over the next 24 hours.

With resolution only two days away, any last-minute shifts in forecast model runs—particularly precipitation timing or cloud cover—could nudge probabilities among the narrow 25–27°C cluster while keeping higher or lower extremes at low implied odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model runs and historical climatology for Karachi in mid-June place the expected daily maximum near 34–36°C under pre-monsoon conditions, with sea-surface temperatures in the northern Arabian Sea and prevailing southwesterly flow moderating extreme heat. Pakistan Meteorological Department observations through June 11 show current highs around 35°C following the dissipation of an earlier heat wave, while ensemble guidance indicates limited daytime warming or slight suppression from increased humidity and possible scattered showers by June 15. These factors concentrate market-implied probability on the 34°C–36°C range, with 35°C holding the plurality at 37 percent as traders weigh the narrow window between typical seasonal peaks and any late-arriving moisture.
